name: MonarchGanttTimeline
title: GanttTimeline
wrapsNative: androidx.compose.ui.layout.SubcomposeLayout (row labels measured first, so rows grow with their text) and androidx.compose.ui.layout.Layout with Modifier.drawWithContent (the grid, gridlines and dependency arrows) in androidx.compose.foundation.horizontalScroll; androidx.compose.foundation.gestures.detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress with HapticFeedbackType for moving and resizing; androidx.compose.material3.TooltipBox with PlainTooltip (milestones); androidx.compose.material3.ListItem, DatePickerDialog and DateRangePicker (the list view); androidx.compose.material3.SingleChoiceSegmentedButtonRow and DropdownMenu (toolbar); MonarchCalendarToolbar, MonarchCollapsible, MonarchButton, MonarchDivider, MonarchText; android.icu.text.DateFormat
summary: Items as bars on a calendar from their first to their last day, with dependency arrows, milestones, a today line, zoom from weeks to years and a list view that writes every date in words and changes dates with the Material 3 date range picker.
whenToUse: To plan and reschedule dated work where overlaps and dependencies matter: tasks, phases or issues with start and due dates, in a project or roadmap screen. Save each onChange as it arrives and pass the new items back.
whenNotToUse: For work that moves through statuses without dates use a board or MonarchStepper. For events at times of day use MonarchAgendaList or a calendar. For one date use the Material 3 DatePicker (see date-picker).

options.name: items
options.description: The rows: id, label, start and end day keys (one of them makes a one-day marker, neither makes it unscheduled), parentId for sub-tasks, groupId, progress from 0 to 1, tone (null is the accent), editable, conflict text and a short meta text.

options.name: previousIcon
options.description: The backward chevron of the toolbar's Earlier button, passed to MonarchCalendarToolbar. Monarch bundles no icons.

options.name: nextIcon
options.description: The forward chevron of the toolbar's Later button.

options.name: state
options.description: The first visible day, the zoom, chart or list, and the collapsed parents. Kept across configuration changes; the app can read and set every value.

options.name: groups
options.description: Heading rows; items with a matching groupId are listed under them. A group with dates shows a thin span on its row.

options.name: dependencies
options.description: Links between items, drawn as arrows (finish to start, start to start or finish to finish) and written as "Depends on" in the list. conflict = true draws the arrow dashed in the danger color.

options.name: milestones
options.description: Dated checkpoints drawn as diamonds: on their item's row with itemId, otherwise in a lane under the header with their name.

options.name: zoomLevels
options.description: The zoom levels offered in the toolbar's zoom menu. With one level or none there is no menu.

options.name: undated
options.description: Top-level items without dates go in an Unscheduled MonarchCollapsible under the chart (List) or stay as chart rows that say "No dates" (Row).

options.name: today
options.description: Any time on the day of the today line, read in timeZone. null hides the line and disables Today. Pass a fixed value in tests and previews.

options.name: timeZone
options.description: The zone today is read in; null is the device's zone. Item dates are always read in UTC. An IANA id such as Europe/Berlin; null, or an id the device does not know, is the device's zone.

options.name: toolbar
options.description: Shows the toolbar: Today, Earlier, Later, the visible range, the zoom menu, the chart and list switch and toolbarActions.

options.name: onChange
options.description: Called once per finished drag, arrow key, TalkBack action or date range picker save, with the item and its new dates as day keys. Without it the timeline is read-only. The timeline never changes items itself.

options.name: onOpen
options.description: Makes each bar and list row a button that opens the item.

options.name: labels
options.description: Replacements for every built-in string, including the bar description, the TalkBack action names and the announcement after a change.

options.name: toolbarActions
options.description: Extra controls at the end of the toolbar, such as a filter or a New item button.

states.name: read only
states.description: Without onChange bars have no drag, no key handling and no TalkBack actions; with onOpen they are still buttons.

states.name: editable
states.description: A visible hint above the chart; each bar can be moved by touch and hold then drag, its ends by holding within 12dp of an end, by the arrow keys and by six TalkBack actions. The list shows Change dates.

states.name: dragging
states.description: The bar follows the finger by whole days with a large shadow, the dependency arrows follow it, and a haptic tick marks each day. Release reports the change once.

states.name: conflict
states.description: The bar uses the danger tone with a dashed 2dp outline; the conflict text is read with the bar and written in the list in the strong danger color.

states.name: one-day marker
states.description: An item with only a start or an end is a small diamond centered on its day; it can only be moved.

states.name: parent
states.description: The row label reads "Hide 2 sub-items" or "Show 2 sub-items" and toggles the children; a parent without dates shows a bracket over its children's span.

states.name: outside the window
states.description: The row says "Ended Jan 9, 2026" or "Starts Mar 2, 2026" instead of a bar.

states.name: unscheduled
states.description: Items without dates are listed in an Unscheduled collapsible under the chart, or as rows saying "No dates".

states.name: list
states.description: One Material 3 ListItem per row with the dates, length, progress, dependencies and conflict in words, then the unscheduled items and the milestones.

appearance: The chart sits on the surface color with a subtle outline; the header, weekends (week and month zoom) and group rows use the subtle background, gridlines and row lines the subtle border. A bar is a light tint of its tone with an outline and a bottom progress strip in the tone's strong fill (accent by default, neutral uses the muted background and the strong border) and its label in the default text color. The today line and its label use the accent fill with accent-on-solid text. Arrows use the subtle text color, or the strong danger color dashed when broken. Done milestones are filled with the accent; open ones are the surface with a muted outline. High contrast themes use their own roles.
platformNotes: There is no iOS GanttTimeline inventory entry yet, so the names follow the web and the plan (MonarchGanttTimeline). The web table view becomes a list (MonarchGanttTimelineView.List) of Material 3 ListItems, the phone and TalkBack pattern; its date inputs become one Change dates button that opens the Material 3 DateRangePicker in a DatePickerDialog. Web pointer drag becomes touch and hold then drag (detectDragGesturesAfterLongPress), so a plain swipe still scrolls the calendar; web keyboard moves stay for hardware keyboards (arrow keys, Shift for the end, Alt for the start, without the web's Up and Down jumps between bars) and are also TalkBack custom actions. The chart scrolls sideways only, not in two axes as the plan said: it does not scroll vertically, so put it in a scrolling screen, and a drag does not scroll the calendar when the finger reaches its edge. The time axis runs left to right in every layout direction, as on the web; the row labels stay at the start. Dates are day keys in epoch milliseconds (UTC midnight) instead of ISO strings, progress is 0 to 1 instead of 0 to 100, and dates are formatted in the configuration's locale. onChange returns nothing: the web's promise with a saving state and rollback is replaced by the app passing new items (or the old ones) back. Zoom, the first visible day, chart or list and the collapsed parents live in a MonarchGanttTimelineState instead of uncontrolled defaults. Tones are MonarchTone with null for the web's accent tone, because MonarchTone has no accent. Title and meta are plain strings, not composable slots, and the conflict has no warning glyph (Monarch bundles no icons): the dashed outline and the words carry it. Experimental because it is a product pattern not yet adopted by a Rook Android app.
accessibility: Each bar is one element read as "<label>, <first day> to <last day>, <n>% complete", with ". Conflict: <message>" when there is a conflict; a one-day marker reads one date.
With onOpen a bar is a button with a 48dp touch target reserved in the layout (the node is at least 48dp wide and as tall as the row, around a narrower visible bar).

Editable bars offer TalkBack custom actions: Move a day earlier, Move a day later, Start a day earlier, Start a day later, End a day earlier, End a day later (markers only the first two). Locked items and read-only timelines offer none.
After a change the new dates are announced through a polite live region on an always-present node: "Design: Jan 12, 2026 to Jan 24, 2026".
A parent's row label is a button with the state Expanded or Collapsed and a visible Hide or Show caption.
The chart and the list are named "Timeline"; group labels are headings; header ticks, the today label and the grid lines are decorative and hidden from TalkBack.
Milestones are images read as "Milestone <name>, <date>" with ", done" when reached; lane milestones also show a plain tooltip on touch and hold.
The list writes every date, length, progress, dependency and conflict, so nothing in the chart depends on dragging, color or position alone.
Rows grow with their label at font scale 2.0, so labels wrap instead of being cut.
edgeCases: Start after end is swapped; dates at any time of day are read as their UTC date.
A drag or key move never lets the first day pass the last when changing one end.
Unknown parent ids, self-parents and parent cycles are ignored; groups that are not listed leave their items at the end.
Bars narrower than five edge zones (60dp) hide their label; every bar is at least 6dp wide on screen.
Items outside the visible window show "Ended …" or "Starts …" in their row.
A dependency to an item that is not shown (collapsed or unscheduled) is not drawn.
Long labels wrap and make their row taller; the bar label inside a bar is cut with an ellipsis but read in full.
The year zoom spans 730 days at 1.6dp a day; the week zoom 28 days at 40dp a day.

examples.title: A read-only plan as a list, with sub-tasks
examples.setup:
val jan5 = 1_767_571_200_000L
val day = 86_400_000L
val state = rememberMonarchGanttTimelineState(initialView = MonarchGanttTimelineView.List)
examples.code:
@OptIn(ExperimentalMonarchApi::class)
MonarchGanttTimeline(
    items = listOf(
        MonarchGanttTimelineItem("build", "Build", start = jan5 + 16 * day, end = jan5 + 39 * day),
        MonarchGanttTimelineItem("api", "API changes", start = jan5 + 21 * day, end = jan5 + 30 * day, parentId = "build"),
        MonarchGanttTimelineItem("launch", "Launch", end = jan5 + 46 * day),
    ),
    previousIcon = {},
    nextIcon = {},
    state = state,
    today = null,
    toolbar = false,
)

parityExceptions.reason: The web's Unscheduled list is a disclosure that starts collapsed: its item names are in the page source but not shown until it is opened. Android starts it collapsed too, as the web does, so "Pricing research" is not on screen in the example.
parityExceptions.convention: a disclosure starts closed on every platform; its items are read once it is opened
